chapter: Quality Serenaders, Cotton Club and union recollections
title: Big bands rehearsing at the union hall
summary: Collette asks whether Ellington and Lunceford rehearsed at the Black union; Howard says they did, and he helped them get started.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: What about some of the events at the union? I know maybe some of these things are hard to remember. See, you've done so much, I think that's just like somebody that's travelled to every city in the world and somebody would say which one did you like the best and it's pretty hard. But you know, at the union on Central, right? Weren't there ever any big bands rehearsing there or you know, if you think back, you know, did Duke Ellington come there or Jimmie Lunceford, just to rehearse?
Duke was there.
Yeah, well, see we want to know about things like this.
Duke was there.
See, we wouldn't know that unless you tell us. What happened there? Was there any activity or something you'd remember?
(Inaudible) no, just--
They used to come there and rehearse?
No, he played.

No, but at the union, because that was the only place for the black bands to -- well, not congregate, you know what I mean, that was their more or less home, because when you'd come in town the unions were separate at that period, and naturally they would kind of get in contact with the black union, and I'm pretty sure some of those bands even had to rehearse there at some point, didn't they?
Yes, they did.
You know, it's like home base. They'd say hey, can you rehearse at the union. So Duke actually rehearsed there, and possibly Jimmie Lunceford?
Yeah, Duke did. He was there, and Jimmie Lunceford.
Sure. That's what I mean, this would possibly happen.
Yeah.
But you would know that, because you probably even okayed it. We'd like to know about some of those things.
I didn't okay it, but --
Well, I mean when they'd want to rehearse --
(Inaudible). I helped them get started.
-- somebody, they had to ask somebody, and you were more or less running that union.
Well, I didn't run the union.
Well, you know what I mean. You knew where everything was and --
I knew where everybody was, but I didn't run it. I tried to stay out of it as much as I could.
But you know, at a time like that if they wanted to rehearse you were probably the one that could say okay, you can use the hall, or something.
Yeah, I tried to. But I --
Yeah, that's what I wanted to know, because I figured those bands would be, you know, coming through there.
I couldn't do it very well.
